note.after_visit_summary: You've been feeling unusually tired for about six weeks, needing naps in the morning and afternoon, which is a change from your usual routine. You also feel dizzy for a moment when you first stand up. We checked your vitals and found your heart rate is slow (52 beats per minute) and your blood pressure drops slightly when you stand. Your ECG showed a slow but normal rhythm with no blockages. After reviewing your medications, we believe your fatigue may be partly due to metoprolol (which can slow the heart) and Tylenol PM (which contains an antihistamine that can cause daytime drowsiness, especially at your age). Here's what we're changing: Stop taking Tylenol PM at night. If you have aches, you can take plain Tylenol (acetaminophen) 500 mg as needed. Reduce your metoprolol from 50 mg to 25 mg twice daily. Keep taking your amlodipine, atorvastatin, and aspirin as before. We're switching your vitamin D to a chewable 1000 unit tablet daily, which should be easier to take. To help with energy and sleep: go to bed and wake up at the same time each day, avoid long afternoon naps, and get some morning light. We drew blood today to check your blood count, kidney and liver function, thyroid, and B12 levels to rule out other causes. When you get up in the morning, sit on the edge of the bed for a minute before standing to avoid dizziness. If you feel faint, have chest pain, or notice your pulse getting slower, call us or go to the emergency room. We'll see you back in two weeks and will call Gloria at 555 -0177 with your lab results.
